standard.title: Create artworks that communicate ideas and meaning
standard.description: use visual conventions, visual arts processes and materials to create artworks that communicate ideas, perspectives and/or meaning
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can use visual conventions, processes and materials to create artworks with deliberate intent (AC9AVA2C01). They make choices about conventions and materials based on communicative purpose. They have not yet planned artworks in advance, used compositional strategies, or created works that communicate specific perspectives.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students use visual conventions, visual arts processes and materials to create artworks that communicate specific ideas, perspectives or meaning — making and explaining deliberate compositional choices.

nodes.label: Generating and selecting ideas
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can generate multiple ideas for an artwork, select one, and document their reason for the selection.
nodes.minimum_width: Generate at least two possible ideas for an artwork and choose one, giving a reason for the choice.
nodes.typical_width: Use mind-mapping, Viewpoints questions and brainstorming to generate multiple compositional ideas linked to a topic; evaluate options and select one; document reasons for selection.
wider: Generate ideas for an artwork inspired by a performance (dance, drama) — explore how to capture movement, gesture or emotion through visual means
Brainstorm how an illustrator's choices in a familiar text communicate perspective — generate and evaluate different ways to illustrate a specific moment
nodes.hinge_reason: Students who cannot generate and evaluate ideas create from the first option that comes to mind. The selection habit is the prerequisite for intentional composition — without it, later nodes about communicating specific perspectives are undermined.

response_modes.reason: Students at this level need structured tools (mind-mapping, Viewpoints questions) to generate genuine options rather than defaulting to one idea immediately. The reasoning move — evaluating and choosing — requires explicit scaffolding.

success_criteria: Generates at least two distinct ideas for an artwork
Selects one and gives a specific reason for the choice (not just 'I like it')

nodes.label: Compositional strategies
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can apply compositional strategies — foreground/background, scale, tone, arrangement — to organise their artwork deliberately.
nodes.minimum_width: Use at least one compositional strategy (e.g. foreground/background, scale, tone) in an artwork and explain how it affects the meaning.
nodes.typical_width: Apply compositional strategies including depth, foreground/middle/background, contrast, arrangement and scale; experiment with how compositional choices change meaning; document and explain choices.
wider: Explore frame-within-frame compositions — experiment with different sized frames to view the world and design compositions that use frames as portals
Investigate how artists from a specific cultural tradition use composition — explore how arrangement serves cultural meaning with guidance from culturally authoritative resources
nodes.hinge_reason: Compositional skills are the craft that makes communicative intent readable to a viewer — students who cannot organise their work compositionally produce artworks that fail to communicate their intended meaning regardless of the quality of the idea.

response_modes.reason: Compositional techniques require practice to become fluent — students need to apply them across multiple works before the choices become natural rather than effortful. Single-exposure teaching at this level produces surface compliance, not genuine skill.

Applying compositional strategies in different contexts (landscape, figure, abstract, response to performance) reveals how the same technique works differently in each — broadening application builds genuine understanding of composition.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Composition is rich because it can be explored across many art forms, contexts and cultural traditions — including cross-arts connections (visual response to dance) and First Nations compositional approaches that offer genuinely different frameworks.
success_criteria: Uses at least one compositional strategy in an artwork
Explains how that strategy affects the work's meaning or impact on the viewer

nodes.label: Creating to communicate a perspective
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can create an artwork that communicates a specific idea, perspective or meaning — combining visual conventions, compositional choices and materials in service of the intent.
nodes.minimum_width: Create an artwork that communicates one idea, perspective or meaning; explain how the visual choices serve that intent.
nodes.typical_width: Create artworks using combinations of visual conventions, processes and materials that communicate specific ideas and perspectives; make and explain deliberate choices; produce artworks that respond to a topic, cross-curricular theme or other arts form.
wider: Create an artwork inspired by a dance or drama — communicate the energy, emotion or narrative through abstract or representational visual means
Apply the compositional approach of an illustrator to communicate a specific perspective on a scene from a familiar text — compare your approach to other students' and to the original

Create an artwork that communicates your personal connection to a place — select visual conventions, symbols and colours that are meaningful to you, informed by reflection on your own cultural background

response_modes.reason: Students bring together idea generation, compositional strategy and material choice into a unified artwork that communicates a specific perspective. The integration move is: all choices serve the communicative intent.

success_criteria: Creates an artwork that communicates a specific idea, perspective or meaning
Explains at least two visual choices (convention, composition, material) in terms of how they serve the communicative intent
